first_supported_failure.last_good: Dark, Light, and System each matched selected UI, stored preference, applied appearance, and panel-document reload.
first_supported_failure.boundary: The T04 baseline-restoration block records only status=failed; its propagated error is replacement_settings_tab_ready_not_observed with matched=0 and visible=0. In source, restoration can call restoreAbsentPreference, then reloadSettings -> Page.reload -> waitForReplacementSettingsTab, before any Settings click. The exact restoration operation/stage and original baseline values are not serialized. Thus the earliest observable concrete failure is Settings-tab readiness after a same-panel reload within restoration, while the first cause may precede that wait.
first_supported_failure.interpretation: The expected extension panel remained reachable, and its shell partly rendered, but the Settings trigger was absent at the readiness timeout. This rules against simple navigation to a different URL or runtime mismatch at the probe instant. It does not establish a Settings product defect or whether the CDP target was replaced with a same-URL target.

cascades_and_coverage: T10/T13 and later section-not-ready results have zero behavior steps; they cannot establish their respective feature defects.
T16/T19/T31/T34/T64 signed-out checks returned false after the T04 boundary; no positive auth-state sample was retained for those checks. Do not infer a sign-in regression.

T22 is marked pass from negative-only admin-control checks, although its warm observation has active=false and sections=[]; the reload observation has active=true. The warm result is not positive guest Settings proof.

T28 passed warm and panel-reload group checks; its full-extension phase was never reached. T40 passed initial and toggle panel-reload checks, then encountered the same reacquisition error later. These later observations suggest intermittent readiness but do not identify cause.
exact_evidence_gap: Original T04 baseline UI/storage sample and selected restoration branch are not in the runner report.

The restore catch replaces the failing observation with status=failed, hiding whether storage mutation, Page.reload, readiness, or baseline comparison failed before the propagated reacquisition error.

No pre/post CDP target identity, timestamped mount transitions, bounded late sample, or captured panel console/runtime error separates a same-URL replacement, delayed boot, and missing-tab render state.

startup_ui_followup.finding: No intentional guest loading screen or AuthGate variant in current source explains five role=tab triggers with zero Settings triggers. AuthGate always renders children, the Settings audience is everyone, and the App tab strip renders a Settings TabsTrigger with title=Settings whenever App renders. The boot waits for persisted settings hydration before mounting React; that pre-mount state would not itself render five tabs.
startup_ui_followup.loading_indicators: The diagnostic counts all #app .animate-spin and .animate-pulse elements, not a named startup marker. App's lazy-tab Suspense fallback has one spinner, and other child features can contribute indicators. Four indicators do not prove which component was loading or that Settings was intentionally absent.
startup_ui_followup.screenshot_limit: native-side-panel.png was captured once after initial guest settle and before exercisePanel, so its five-icon shell with loading placeholders is not a screenshot of the T04 failure. It cannot be paired with the later zero-Settings DOM probe.
startup_ui_followup.remaining_discriminator: The failure probe does not serialize titles/locations of its five role=tab elements or an App shell identifier. Thus they cannot be identified as the five public App strip tabs; if they were those exact tabs, Settings should be one. Capture sanitized tab-title membership and parent strip identity at the same failure instant, alongside the prior target identity and runtime/error samples.

minimal_next_experiment: On the same frozen artifact in a fresh guest profile, run only the T04 sequence once. Keep behavior assertions unchanged. Serialize a sanitized initial baseline (selected/stored/presence), restoration stage and storage after the restoration write, plus pre/post target identity equality, Settings-tab count, loading count, and a timestamped transition at the existing readiness deadline and one bounded later observation. Capture panel console/runtime errors at that boundary. Then discriminate: a late Settings mount on the same target implicates boot timing; permanent absence with stable target and app error implicates panel rendering; changed target identity implicates reacquisition. Do not merely widen the timeout or infer a product fix from the current report.
